shots.visual_event: Nila steps off the train at a glass tower built where her 1913 railway cottage once stood.
Through clock-light she overlays the old cottage on the lobby; Devika sets a dinner place but cannot see her daughter.
The memory repeats Devika asking why there is an extra plate, confirming Nila was erased the moment she boarded.
Meera approaches without a weapon and places her turquoise clip beside Nila’s bare foot as proof of a remembered person.
shots.dialogue_audio: Meera: “Being remembered by force is not coming home.”

shots.visual_event: Nila’s grief sends a shock through the engine; citizens nearby lose their most cherished memories and become emotionally blank.
shots.dialogue_audio: Nila: “Then nobody gets to keep what I lost.”

shots.visual_event: Arin reaches Nila but cannot touch her through the storm of stolen memories.
shots.dialogue_audio: Arin: “I know what it is to trade yourself for a sister.”

end_card.text: THE VILLAIN WAS A CHILD WHO CAME HOME TOO LATE
